what_its_for: Somatropin is a man-made version of human growth hormone. It is used to help children who are not growing properly due to low growth hormone levels or certain medical conditions. In adults, it helps replace growth hormone when the body does not make enough, which can improve energy, body composition, and bone strength. It may also be used for other conditions your doctor has prescribed it for.
how_to_take: Somatropin is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous) or sometimes into a muscle, depending on the brand and your doctor's instructions. Your doctor, nurse, or pharmacist will show you exactly how to give the injection. Common injection sites include the belly (abdomen), thighs, upper arms, or buttocks. Rotate your injection sites each time to avoid lumps or skin irritation. Use a new needle and syringe every time. Do not shake the medication — gently swirl or roll it if mixing is needed. Always check the liquid before injecting; it should be clear and colorless. Do not use it if it looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles in it.
dosing: Your dose is carefully calculated by your doctor based on your body weight, age, medical condition, and how you respond to treatment. Doses are different for children and adults, and for different conditions. Most people inject somatropin once a day, often in the evening before bedtime because growth hormone is naturally released during sleep. Never change your dose on your own. Follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up to make up for a missed dose. If you miss several doses in a row, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store unmixed (unreconstituted) somatropin in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it. Keep it away from direct light. Once mixed (reconstituted), storage instructions vary by brand — some must be used right away, others can be refrigerated for up to 14 to 28 days. Check the specific instructions that come with your brand. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used needles in an approved sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid injecting into skin that is red, bruised, sore, or hard. Do not freeze the medication or leave it out at room temperature for too long. Avoid starting somatropin if you have an active serious illness, recent surgery, or a serious injury without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as somatropin can interact with steroids, insulin, and thyroid medications. Avoid alcohol in excess, as it can affect how well the medication works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe headache, vision changes, or nausea and vomiting (signs of increased pressure in the brain); hip or knee pain or a limp in children; sudden stomach pain; numbness or tingling in your hands or wrists; signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurred vision; skin reactions at the injection site that do not go away; swelling of the hands, feet, or ankles; unusual tiredness or weakness; or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing.
when_it_works: Somatropin does not work overnight. In children being treated for growth problems, noticeable growth may take several months. Most doctors check progress every 3 to 6 months. In adults, improvements in energy, body composition, and bone density may take 6 months to a year or longer. It is important to keep all follow-up appointments and lab tests so your doctor can monitor how well the treatment is working and adjust your dose if needed.
special_populations: Children: Somatropin is commonly used in children with growth hormone deficiency or other growth-related conditions. Dosing is based on body weight and must be adjusted regularly as the child grows. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of somatropin during pregnancy is not well established. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to the effects and side effects of somatropin, so lower starting doses may be used. Patients with diabetes: Somatropin can raise blood sugar levels, so blood glucose monitoring may need to be increased and diabetes medications may need adjustment. Patients with thyroid or adrenal problems: Somatropin can affect other hormone levels, so your doctor may need to monitor or adjust your other hormone treatments.
